advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make test_a_monkeypatch_on_config_still_reaches_a_real_consumer actually invoke the real consumer (drive attest.py's signing path, or a runner call) so a repointed import fails it, rather than re-executing config's import binding inside the test.
evidence: tests/unit/test_gate_context_seam.py:155-158: `monkeypatch.setattr(llm_config, "current_code_sha", lambda: "deadbeef")` then `from rebar.llm.config import current_code_sha as resolved_at_call_time` then `assert resolved_at_call_time() == "deadbeef"`

Docstring claims: 'Structure tests can pass while this fails if a consumer was quietly repointed.' (line 151-152) — but the test never imports or calls attest.py; it only replicates config's import pattern locally.

attest.py:122-125 does its OWN `from rebar.llm.config import current_code_sha` and calls `current_code_sha()`; the test does not route through this code, so repointing attest to gate_context would not fail it.

The actual behavioural proof already exists at tests/unit/test_provider_session_guard.py:162-185, which patches `llm_config.assert_gated` and drives it through the real consumer PydanticAIRunner.run — the pattern this new test claims to add but does not.
advisory.finding: test_a_monkeypatch_on_config_still_reaches_a_real_consumer does not exercise the real consumer it names (plan_review/attest.py:123). It re-executes the same `from rebar.llm.config import current_code_sha` binding inside the test body and asserts on THAT, instead of invoking attest. It would still pass if attest.py were repointed to import from rebar.llm.gate_context — the exact silent-break failure mode the test's own docstring claims to catch — so it is regression-blind to the contract it exists for.
advisory.suggested_fix: Call into the real consumer under the patch — e.g. patch rebar.llm.config.current_code_sha to a sentinel and invoke the attest signing entry point that does the function-level import, asserting the observable effect (the sentinel SHA reaches the signed attestation / the None-SHA refusal is bypassed). This exercises attest.py:123's binding so a repoint to gate_context fails.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the source-text grep in test_the_seam_headroom_bounds_are_per_file with an import/behavioral check of the sibling's per-file bounds (e.g. import _LOC_BOUNDS and assert each file maps to its own bound) rather than asserting the absence of a literal loop string.
evidence: tests/unit/test_gate_context_seam.py:167-169: reads test_plan_review_workflow_ops_seam.py as text and asserts `"for path in (_WORKFLOW_OPS, _LLM_CONFIG)" not in seam`

The grepped token is a test-source string, not a contract read by any non-human consumer; the actual per-file behavior is already asserted structurally by _LOC_BOUNDS in test_plan_review_workflow_ops_seam.py:64-67.
advisory.finding: test_the_seam_headroom_bounds_are_per_file asserts by grepping the SIBLING TEST file's source text for the absence of the literal string 'for path in (_WORKFLOW_OPS, _LLM_CONFIG)'. This couples to the sibling test's implementation wording, not its behavior: renaming the path constants or reformatting the loop would break/pass the guard with no change to whether the bounds are actually per-file, making it a change-detector over test source.
advisory.suggested_fix: Import _LOC_BOUNDS from test_plan_review_workflow_ops_seam and assert it contains (_LLM_CONFIG, 700) and that config.py is asserted below 700 — a behavioral check that survives reformatting of the sibling loop.
